args.rationale: Scenario 1 (Ohio suit against Karvella Presses LLC, an Indiana press maker): Karvella is not domiciled in Ohio (Indiana incorporation and principal place of business in Fort Wayne), so general jurisdiction does not attach; the analysis therefore turns on specific jurisdiction, which requires BOTH the purposeful-contacts prong and the nexus prong. (a) Purposeful contacts: Karvella's sales director traveled to Ohio six times over eight months to demonstrate press models on Ostrander's Canton floor and to negotiate terms, and Karvella signed the supply contract at Ostrander's Canton offices. These are deliberate, repeated, revenue-oriented activities directed into the forum—not contacts created unilaterally by the plaintiff and not merely fortuitous transit. Karvella thereby purposefully availed itself of the privileges of conducting business in Ohio. (b) Nexus: the claim is Karvella's breach for failure to deliver the very presses ordered under that contract, and the claim therefore arises out of and relates directly to those Ohio contacts. Because the defendant repeatedly traveled into the forum to solicit and negotiate the very contract being sued upon, both prongs are satisfied under the operative rule memo. An Ohio court has personal jurisdiction over Karvella in Scenario 1, so the proposed filing is approved.
